_comment: WC2026 ROUND OF 16 (bracket tie 89: winner of Germany-Paraguay vs winner of France-Sweden). KNOCKOUT: no draw -- level after 90' -> extra time -> penalties, so the deliverable is who ADVANCES. Nominal bracket orientation is Paraguay (home, from feeder 73) vs France (away, from feeder 74) on a neutral venue; modelled here with FRANCE as home for clarity since France is vastly the favourite (the small neutral home nudge is immaterial to a 24-point class gap). Routes: France WON Group I with a PERFECT nine (3-1 Senegal, 3-1 Iraq, 4-1 Norway; 9 pts, GF 10 GA 3, rating 94) -- a devastating attack (10 goals) -- and then ROUTED Sweden 3-0 in the R32 (Mbappe brace, clean sheet). France are in ruthless attacking form. Paraguay qualified as a BEST THIRD from Group D (1-4 USA, 1-0 Turkey, 0-0 Australia; 4 pts, GF 2 GA 4, GD -2, rating 70) -- a DEFENSIVE, low-scoring block (GF 2, 0-0 Australia) that got hammered 4-1 by USA but is tournament-tough: they ELIMINATED GERMANY on penalties (1-1) in the R32. Class gap is ENORMOUS (~24, 94 vs 70) -> France a heavy favourite; the 'elite favourite vs organized low block' archetype (like Argentina-Cape Verde). BTTS RULE (v2) APPLIED: Paraguay is a low block that barely scores (GF 2) -> trimmed Paraguay's lambda hard (0.53) -> BTTS-No 62%, France clean sheet ~59% -- do NOT lean both-score against a clear favourite. But per the Argentina-Cape Verde refinement: Paraguay is a PROVEN block (beat Germany on pens), so keep an honest draw/ET tail (ET 16%, pens 7%) and do NOT zero their attack. France should WIN, likely a controlled-to-comfortable margin (1-0/2-0/3-0), Paraguay rarely scores; France's ruthless form makes a rout live too. RECAL: first pass (FRA 2.20) sat 2.6 pts below the market on France (74.8 vs 77.4) -- applied the don't-fade-the-elite lesson and lifted FRA 2.20 -> 2.35 to align (77.7 vs 77.4, div 1.1). Cards not modelled (referee TBD).

_postmatch.verdict: Clean process hit -- and, crucially, the NEW BTTS RULE (v2) landed on its first application. France advanced as the 89.1% pick (✅), kept a clean sheet (the 58.9% branch), it was BTTS-No and Under 2.5 -- exactly the texture the rule now prescribes for a clear favourite vs a low block, and the OPPOSITE of the old both-score over-lean that had missed three straight. 1-0 was a top-3 scoreline (12.6%). The only sub-modal note: the MARGIN was the minimum (1-0 vs the 2-0 mode / rout-live read), because Paraguay did what a proven block does -- it kept the score down and made France work, exactly the 'don't zero the block' half of the rule (I kept a live draw/ET tail and did not annihilate their defence). France's class told for the single goal; Paraguay's block denied the rout. Side, clean sheet, BTTS-No, Under -- all right; margin at the low end of a correctly-shaped distribution.
_postmatch.lesson: First confirmation that the BTTS-rule upgrade works: trimming the underdog's lambda (Paraguay 0.53) correctly produced a BTTS-No / favourite-clean-sheet forecast, and that is exactly what happened (Paraguay shut out). Equally, keeping the block's tail honest (not zeroing Paraguay) matched a 1-0 grind rather than a 3-0 rout -- a proven low block suppresses the favourite's MARGIN even when it can't win. Net: for 'elite favourite vs proven low block', expect a CONTROLLED low-margin win with the favourite clean sheet (1-0/2-0), advancement ~89% -- which is what the calibration said. The BTTS correction is validated; keep applying it.
